words: إن الله قد حكم بين العباد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God judges the servants justly, placing the people of Paradise and Hell in their respective homes; no one can benefit another.
rows.anchor: فلا يغني أحد عن أحد شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing their distance from God and unfitness to address Him, Hell's inhabitants turn their hopes to the angels as intermediaries.
rows.anchor: ليسوا بأهل لدعائه سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those asking the guardians include all the people in Hell, both followers and those followed.
rows.anchor: أي جميعا الأتباع والمتبوعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming Hell instead of using a pronoun evokes its layer and grimacing guardians, showing the damned's misery and inability to put things in their proper place, as in worldly life.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أن سؤالهم لأهل الطبقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask for one day's worth of relief from only part of the punishment.
rows.anchor: يخفف عنه يوما } أي مقداره { من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardians expose why the damned are cast aside and unworthy of a hearing: they had received messengers bearing clear proofs.
rows.anchor: الجاعل لهم في محل الاطراح والسفول عن التأهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardians rebuke them for failing to use reason and for wasting the time when answered prayer might have helped.
rows.anchor: إلزامنا لهم الحجة وتوبيخا وتنديما بتفويت أوقات الدعاء المجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn is omitted from تك, while the imperfect تأتيكم depicts the messengers' successive, repeated coming.
rows.anchor: بإسقاط النون مع التصوير للحال بالمضارع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their messengers were human beings from among them, so they should have listened; people are more receptive to their own kind.
rows.anchor: أي الذين هم منكم فأنتم جديرون بالإصغاء إليهم والإقبال عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers came with proofs clearer than anything else.
rows.anchor: أي التي لا شيء أوضح منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Hell admit that the messengers did come to them with such proofs.
rows.anchor: أي أتونا كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardians tell them to pray now, whether to God or to God's human messengers, angels, or others; alternatively, they tell them to stop because no one will hear them.
rows.anchor: أي أنتم الآن الله أو أهل الله من رسل البشر أو الملائكة أو غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are those who veil their faculties of reason from the light of reason supported by sound transmission.
rows.anchor: الساترين لمرائي عقولهم عن أنوار العقل المؤيد بصحيح النقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prayer goes nowhere, as their worldly deeds did: this life is the Hereafter's field, and the harvest there is of the kind planted here.
rows.anchor: أي ذهاب في غير طريق موصل كما كانوا هم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawāʾ means balance or justice, neither more nor less than half, and grammatically calls for two terms; he illustrates it with Qurʾān 3:64.
rows.anchor: الذي هو بمعنى العدل الذي لا يزيد عن النصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He construes sawāʾ as an accusative verbal noun: the provision and blessing are apportioned evenly across two days and two days.
rows.anchor: أي التوزيع إلى يومين ويومين على السواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase addresses those who ask, or are disposed to investigate how this verse's apparent meaning accords with other verses.
rows.anchor: أي لمن سأل أو كان بحيث يسأل ويشتد بحثه بسؤال أو نظر

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads sawāʾ in the genitive, making it an adjective qualifying the four days.
rows.anchor: معينة لأن تكون نعتا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads sawāʾ in the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: وقراءة أبي جعفر بالرفع خبر لمبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Burjān relates the four days of completing the earth and its provisions to the four seasons, with rain from heaven sustaining earthly life.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى الأمر إلى السماء أولا في إنزال الماء

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Burjān names winter, spring, summer, and autumn as the observable seasons in which sowing and the earth's benefits are completed.
rows.anchor: فيهن يتم زرع الأرض وبركات الدنيا

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Burjān takes al-sāʾilīn as an expression of wonder and strangeness that magnifies the addressee's significance.
rows.anchor: تعجيب وإغراب وتعظيم للمراد المعنى بالخطاب

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Burjān also relates sawāʾ to the year's balance in celestial risings, settings, distances, elevations, and northward and southward courses.
rows.anchor: أن بهذه الأربعة الأيام استوت السنة مطالعها ومغاربها وقربها وبعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then marks the heavens' greater scale and importance than the earth, along with God's great care for them.
rows.anchor: ولفظ الاستواء وحب الغاية الدال على عظيم العناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains istawā ilā as directing an intentional purpose toward the heaven and bringing that purpose to completion.
rows.anchor: أي قصد قصدا هو القصد منتهيا قصده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heaven was smoke, understood as water vapor and figuratively compared in appearance to smoke rising from fire; the actions of forming earth and completing heaven's benefits overlap.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك الدخان بخار الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heaven preceded the earth in its smoky state; the counted periods overlap because the creative actions overlap.
rows.anchor: فالسماء متقدمة في الدخانية على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth must release their entrusted benefits, such as water, plants, and minerals, at their appointed times and proper measures, willingly or unwillingly under compulsion rather than legal obligation.
rows.anchor: في إخراج ما أودعتكما من الأمانة في أوقاتها وعلى ما ينبغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two respond that they and what they contain submit completely, neither withholding nor changing what God commands.
rows.anchor: أي في كل ما رسمته فينا لا نحمل من ذلك شيئا بل نبذله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two are addressed and speak as rational beings; the masculine plural طائعين treats them together with the rational creatures within them.
rows.anchor: قال جامعا لهما باعتبار أفرادهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual form of their reply does not require the address to have occurred simultaneously; God may have addressed them in succession.
rows.anchor: لا يدل على جمعه في الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their obedience is their delivery of the entrusted benefits, rather than their bearing that trust themselves.
rows.anchor: وذلك هو بذلهما للأمانة , وعدم حملها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses fa-qaḍāhunna as creating and fashioning the seven heavens with an effective, unerring act like a decree.
rows.anchor: أي خلقهن وصنعهن حال كونهن معدودات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two days assigned to the heavens are Thursday and Friday, counted as their share of the six days of creating the two realms.
rows.anchor: أي الخميس والجمعة إذا حسب مقدار ما يخصهن من التكوين في الستة الأيام

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarīr says Friday was named because God gathered the creation of the heavens and earth on that day, meaning He completed it.
rows.anchor: وإنما سمي يوم الجمعة لأن الله تعالى جمع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains revelation as a hidden communication and decisive command, assigning each heaven its governing order and benefits in a firm system.
rows.anchor: أي الأمر الذي دبرها ودبر منافعها به على نظام محكم لا يختل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearest heaven is adorned for people with shining stars, though their radiance showing through does not rule out their being in higher heavens.
rows.anchor: من زواهر النجوم , وشفوفها عنها لا ينافي أن تكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses rhetorical ellipsis: the verbal noun حفظا implies an omitted verb of protection, while the decoration phrase implies its corresponding verb.
rows.anchor: حذف فعل الحفظ بدلالة المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This wondrous arrangement is the decree of the invincible God, who overcomes all, and the all-knowing God, whose knowledge encompasses everything.
rows.anchor: المحيط علما بكل شيء وكما قدر سبحانه ذلك بعزته وعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing names promise the addressed community a share of God's might and knowledge, especially in gifts and natural dispositions, beyond earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: بشارة للأمة التي خوطبت بهما أنه يوتيها من عزه وعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation unfolded over six days rather than an instant to refute the notion that God acts by nature rather than choice; six is a perfect number, its proper divisors summing to it.
rows.anchor: لو خلقه في لمحة لكان ذلك شبهة لمن يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's two periods, counted for its substance and benefits, allude to shirk as a doubling; the heavens' signs more clearly establish divine unity and their inhabitants did not incur that warning.
rows.anchor: ولم يكرر في السماء لأن آياتها أدل على التوحيد ولم يحصل من أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That the greater, more intricate heavens were made in less time than the earth further demonstrates God's free choice through wondrous wisdom.
rows.anchor: مع أنها أكبر جرما وأعجب صنعا وأتقن جسما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears every sound, including a plea for refuge, and knows every matter, including Satan's prompting; He can thwart it, unlike powerless deaf and mute idols.
rows.anchor: الذي يسمع كل مسموع من استعاذتك وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the polytheists' idols and the virtue of prayer, the author presents cosmic signs as proofs of monotheism that dispel all rivals and illuminate God's essence and attributes through His acts.
rows.anchor: أتبعه دلائل التوحيد إعلاما بأن التوحيد أحسن الحسن يطرد كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day, sun and moon are signs of God's oneness; their arrangement demonstrates power over resurrection and every possible thing.
rows.anchor: أي الدالان باختلافهما وهيئتهما على قدرته على البعث وعلى كل مقدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night precedes day because darkness is nonexistence and light is existence; the sun and moon are like the spirit of night and day, their bodies.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت الظلمة عدما والنور وجودا والعدم مقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poetic saying calls the created universe a message from the highest King to humanity and says everything besides God is vain.
rows.anchor: تأمل سطور الكائنات فإنها من الملك الأعلى إليك رسائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated negation stresses that each object is separately forbidden, and the moon is named explicitly instead of being left to a pronoun.
rows.anchor: أعاد النافي تأكيدا للنفي لأن النهي عن كل منهما على حدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun is described as the greatest of the worshippers' idols, though it too is one of God's created things.
rows.anchor: التي هي أعظم أوثانكم فإنها من جملة مبدعاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God, possessor of every perfection without defect, deserves prostration because He created the four signs; the feminine plural pronoun follows the convention for inanimate things and underscores their lowliness as deities.
rows.anchor: أي الأربعة لأجلكم فهو الذي يستحق الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He entertains another explanation for the feminine plural: the moon is counted as multiple moons because it changes through crescent, full, and dark phases.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون عد القمر أقمارا لأنه يكون تارة هلالا وأخرى بدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True worship must belong exclusively to God: prostrating even once to another makes the worship shirk, and God accepts only sincere worship because He is utterly self-sufficient.
rows.anchor: فإن أشركتم به شيئا بسجود أو غيره فما خصصتموه بالعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that they worship idols only to bring them nearer to God (39:3) conflicts with their own exclusive invocations in distress, especially at sea.
rows.anchor: كما هو صريح قولكم في الدعاء في وقت الشدائد لا سيما في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse urges people to preserve human dignity by never prostrating to a creature: angels were commanded to prostrate to Adam, while Iblīs refused, marking opposite stations.
rows.anchor: أمر الملائكة الذين هم أشرف خلقه بعدهم بالسجود آدم وهم في ظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those deeply entrenched in disbelief are barred by it from repentance and faith, face severe punishment, and do not have their prayers answered; other sinners' punishment need not be severe.
rows.anchor: الذين منعتهم عراقتهم من التوبة والإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses antithetical ellipsis: mentioning acceptance first implies its opposite for disbelievers, and the latter's punishment implies the contrasting case for sinners; the arrangement gives a motive to obey and a deterrent from sin.
rows.anchor: ذكر الاستجابة أولا دليلا على ضدها ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine response does not mean granting every worldly request as specified: abundant grants often breed arrogance and misery, defeating the supplicant's purpose.
rows.anchor: الإجابة إلى كل ما يسأل بأن يكون في هذه الدار يؤدي في الغالب إلى البطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says a prayer may be answered by granting the request, averting a comparable affliction, or deferring its reward to the Hereafter; the author gives no transmitter or grading.
rows.anchor: وتارة تكون بدفع مثله من البلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine name emphasizes the greatness of the matter, which requires full knowledge of human traits and the power to give or withhold.
rows.anchor: أي الملك الأعظم الجامع لجميع صفات الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God gave all servants, repentant and otherwise, more than they needed, they would pursue every desire by force like powerful kings, multiplying killing, plunder, and other corruption.
rows.anchor: أي لصاروا يريدون كل ما يشتهونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God apportions provision for people collectively and individually, not exceeding or falling short of the measure He sets, according to His wisdom.
rows.anchor: أي بتقدير لهم جملة ولكل واحد منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording encompasses all servants, not just those made wealthy or constrained; God knows their outward and inward states and arranges each person's situation and its causes accordingly.
rows.anchor: يعلم جميع ظواهر أمورهم وحركاتهم وانتقالاتهم وكلامهم وبواطنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone sends rain by choice; this counters those who attribute rainfall, vegetation, and crops to a habitual process of time.
rows.anchor: بين أنه سبحانه هو الفاعل لذلك بقدرته واختياره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses the pronoun of the unseen because sending rain is one of the keys of the unseen.
rows.anchor: معبرا بالضمير الذي هو غيب لأجل أن إنزال الغيث من مفاتيح الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghayth is rain that brings succor: people receive what they asked for and are relieved outwardly, just as revelation relieves them outwardly and inwardly.
rows.anchor: المطر الي يغاث به الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain comes after people have despaired of it and realized that no one else can send it, making them more inclined to give thanks.
rows.anchor: يئسوا من إنزاله وعملوا انه لا يقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the rain mercy broadens its effects: it spreads over plains and mountains and produces pools, rivers, vegetation, trees, grain, fruit, and other benefits.
rows.anchor: على السهل والجبل فينزل من السحاب المحمول بالريح من الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The softness of plants brought from hard soil and delicate branches from rough trees show God's power; denying resurrection or evading it is therefore foolish.
rows.anchor: فما أجلف من ينكر إخراجه الموتى من القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After rejecting the taking of patrons besides God and affirming that He alone is the Patron (42:9), the author points to rain and its effects as evidence of His care.
rows.anchor: أنكر عليهم فيما مضى اتخاذ ولي من دونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Walī is the one closest to His servants in every matter; al-Ḥamīd deserves every kind of praise and rewards obedience with increasing bounty and enduring closeness.
rows.anchor: الذي لا أحد أقرب منه إلى عباده في شيء من الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The measured provision and rain are among God's signs of power and free choice, part of how He enlivens existence through revelation and physical things such as water.
rows.anchor: فذلك من آيات الله الدالة على قدرته واختياره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens, earth, and their benefits display God's power; what He spreads through them includes varied living bodies, hearts, capacities, forms, and traits.
rows.anchor: أي فرق بالأبدان والقلوب على هذا المنوال الغريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because earth is a base and heaven its roof, something located in either can be said to be in both; each contributes through its contents and elements.
rows.anchor: فمن كان في أحدهما صح نسبته إلى أنه في كل منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dābba means any living thing capable of movement, including humans, jinn, and the many kinds of animals.
rows.anchor: أي شيء فيه أهلية الدبيب بالحياة من الإنس والجن وسائر الحيوانات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Observing God's crafts establishes His existence, power, and choice; sustained reflection leads to knowledge of His names, attributes, what is due or impossible for Him, and the wisdom brought by the messengers and books.
rows.anchor: تيقن وجوده وقدرته واختياره
